[b]January 30, 2028: Senate Committee Building, Closed Door Meeting[/b]

Gentlemen, thank you for attending to this meeting, began Edis Behic, walking into the boardroom where the 14 senators for Yzak Now! Were assembled, they nodded and replied in varied forms of acknowledgement as Edis sat down, an aide quietly handing him some papers.

Now, as you know, the Shah and Prelate are out of the country for a special visit to our allies, and as such, I have decided to take the initiative to discuss a new bill which has appeared in the Chamber of the People, one which the Shah sees as crucial to his debt program. He paused and waited for a comment before continuing.

Now, the bill in question seeks to slash excess spending in the administration of the government, culling various offices and potentially entire sections of the government, he said.

It is a dangerous bill, Edis, intoned one of the Senators, The bill you refer to proposes, for my colleagues who are not familiar, it proposes major cuts to the department of education, the ministry of labour, the ministry of social development, the ministry of capital affairs, stated the Senator, counting off his fingers the list.
Not just cuts, replied another senator, He intends a mass-merger, into a new department, 

Yes, the Department of Societal Affairs, under the bill, the departments which Senator Ihzak listed off would be folded into one department, replied Edis, pulling out a sharpie marker and writing on the white board that sat behind him. 

So would the departments in question remain under this proposed department, or would the department itself run every aspect? inquired a Senator.

The bill is intentionally vague on that; its one of the reasons your colleagues in the Chamber havent yet managed to pull forward a majority vote, replied Edis.

Its an absurd proposition, I do not see how it will lower debt, said Ihzak.

No, you are right, and I believe the bill should die on the floor, replied Edis, Frankly, the debt we have is as a result of systems which havent been updated since the era of the Shah Zeki, 

The others nodded.

It is thus that I would like to push the Senate to adopt a five-year debt reduction plan that will be presented to the Chamber in a special session. We need 2/3rds for a special session in the Chamber, and thus we can, without a doubt, hit this out of the park with our party majority. Said Edis.

And what is this plan? Asked one of the senators.

The five-year debt reduction plan will begin with a freeze on wage growth and government hiring within 2028. We intend to go through the various offices and remove unnecessary programs and hires within the offices. In 2028, we will also push within this plan to create a simplified industrial permit system, and a push for the port companies and shipping companies to optimise port operations, Rattled off Edis.

I assume transparency will also be a major pillar? asked Ihzak.

Yes, replied Edis.
A few frowns crossed the faces of the senators. That would play into the hands of the left, are you aware of this? asked Ihzak.

Yes, I think we should push for a coalition to pass this, eliminate the right-wing dissent in the Chamber and Senate, replied Edis.

But thatd risk the right-wing taking to the streets and utilising the institutional memory of the revolution to sway the polls, intoned a concerned Senator.

I have spoken with the Prelate of the Chamber, and he said hed be able to hash out a smaller deal from within the bill that should appease the right, replied Edis.

Anyways, I have to go now, so your offices can submit any excess questions that you have to my secretary, stated Edis, checking his watch and beginning to pack up. Dismissed, he said with a smile.

[quote=nordiheim;61348489][spoiler=A meeting in Nordiheim]
When the group from the Lavian air combat procurement command (LACPC) arrived in Nordiheim they were greeted by Nordiheim's minister of war, Grand general Thormod Thormodson III, together with the commanders of the airforce and navy branches of the military.
As part of their visit the LACPC group was given a tour of the KJ-8A Black Swan and some of its local facilities in the Midland region as well as a test flight to showcase the aircraft's aerial abilities when in the hands of an experienced pilot, even a short showing of the most current prototype of the 8AC was shown off to display how it was not too far away from production and use.

Later during the talks it was laid forth by the minister of war that Nordiheim was both interested in allowing them to buy the KJ-8A, and its 8AC variant when finished, but also that they in turn was interested in acquiring the Lavian F-150 Diamondback for their own airforce as Nordiheim was currently lacking a dedicated air superiority fighter of their own.
It was also proposed a mutual permission and licence agreement between the two nations in regards to these aircraft when it came to the logistics, maintenance, operation and sharing of any upgrades developed for them over time by either nation, assuming continued friendly relations between them of course.

 A potential cooperation in the development of future aircraft projects was also allowed to float around during the talks in the interest of ensuring that both nations' air forces would continue to be able to keep up with global aerial technology and developments by combining their resources and research to potentialy create the next generation of aircraft in a timely manner so that they wouldnt risk falling behind other nations.
[/spoiler][/quote]

[b]New deal signed between major Argos military producers![/b]

In a groundmaking deal today, the Lavian ACPC and Nordiheim's Minister of War have both announced that the ULR and Nordiheim have created the Joint-Initiative Aircraft Research and Development program. The program focuses on both nations cooperating in 5th gen aircraft development, integrated aircraft systems, and exporting existing 5th gen aircraft to each other. Both parties plan to jointly license aircraft production to each other, the ULR buying the KJ-8A Black Swan and Nordiheim buying the F-150 Diamondback.  

Analysts deeply believe that information gathered from both aircraft included in the deal will go into improving the second generation of the Black Swan jet which is already in its prototype phase, the KJ-8AC. Even though the prototype is already conducting powered trials, reportedly even being flown during the KJ-8A demonstration for the ACPC as well as being slated for production, information as well as design changes are possible before official production begins. 

Most countries slightly degrade the quality of their avionics and systems on their exports, including both the ULR and Nordiheim, but this deal lays out complete technology sharing related to both aircraft, as well as collaborating to further upgrade systems in both compatibility and general usefulness. Time will tell how the deal and development goes, but nonetheless this deal is a landmark for native Argos military aviation.
